newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains stock jumps on upbeat earnings; cuts 215 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains stock jumps on upbeat earnings; cuts 215 jobs.

text.p: The stock of Earthgrains Co. jumped Monday after the maker of fresh baked goods reported better-than-expected results for the latest quarter and announced a plant shutdown that will cut 215 jobs.
Earthgrains, which was spun off from Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc. last March, was up $2.625 at $50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The St. Louis-based company said it earned $9.2 million, or 91 cents a share, in its fiscal third quarter ended Dec. 31, compared with a loss of $9.3 million, or 91 cents a share, a year earlier.
The gain for the quarter came despite a drop in sales to $522.7 million from $525.0 million.
Earthgrains also announced that it will close its Indianapolis refrigerated dough plant by the end of March and transfer production to a plant in Carrollton, Texas.
A company spokesman said 215 employees at the plant will lose their jobs, and five to 10 managers will be relocated.
Earthgrains said it will take a charge of $6 million to $8 million in the fourth quarter for the plant closure.
"Our turnaround progress is on track, and we anticipate additional long-term improvements," Barry Beracha, chairman, said in a statement.

"Price increases taken during the year for fresh baked goods have continued to hold," he said. "Additionally, we have been an active participant in industry consolidation and look forward to continuing these efforts."
The third quarter also benefited from strong seasonal sales and prices increases for U.S. refrigerated dough products.
